stances.summary: Labor market resilient despite recent weakness
stances.quote: Bottom line: Compared to what we thought yesterday the outlook is a tiny bit weaker (which is what the markets are reacting to). But compared to what we thought a month or two or three ago this is a remarkably resilient and stable labor market even in the face of big shocks.

stances.summary: Wage gains positive for workers, concerning for Fed's inflation mandate
stances.quote: Finally, the price data have been increasingly concerning about the trajectory of inflation but the wage data have been reassuring. But June was a tick in the direction of good for workers but more concerning for the Fed and its price stability mandate.

stances.summary: Employment data shows mixed signals between survey sources
stances.quote:
The participation rate fell a lot in June along with EPOP--including EPOP for prime age workers.

The household and payroll surveys telling very different stories--and the household one itself internally inconsistent. Generally means go with payroll but worth looking more.

stances.summary: Unemployment stability at low level historically unusual and notable
stances.quote: Two years ago the unemployment rate was 4.1%, now its 4.2%. That is almost unheard of to plateau at a low level like that--and even more so to have adjusted up from about 3.5% without continuing up.

stances.summary: Jobs data mixed; employment gains modest, unemployment stable, participation declined
stances.quote:
Jobs day:

57K jobs added in June (111K average for last three months), less than expected but probably more than breakeven.

Unemployment rate fell to 4.2%, has been stable for 2 years now, but participation and employment rates fell.

Wage growth picked up.

stances.summary: Characterizes inflation metrics as elevated and concerning
stances.quote: PCE-based ecumenical underlying inflation measure was 3.5% in May. As most metrics are highly elevated.

stances.summary: Employment strong, inflation risk asymmetrically concerning
stances.quote: But this plus the upward revision in Q1 GDP to 2.1% annual rate (from 1.6% annual rate in the second estimate) overall suggests there is very little reason to be concerned about the employment side of the mandate but substantial and asymetric on the inflation side.

stances.summary: Market slowdown and wage deceleration support dovish Fed case
stances.quote: But, the dove case is that market-based is slowing. And outside this release, that wage growth continues to slow and is generally consistent with about 2.5% inflation.

stances.summary: Flags economic data slide as particularly concerning
stances.quote: And this was the most concerning slide of the data this past month.

stances.summary: PCE inflation elevated with worrying broadbased price pressures
stances.quote:
PCE inflation came in high. And the details were even more worrying than the headline as the risk of inflation mounting outside the tariff/Iran affected sectors.

Core PCE annual rate:
1 month: 3.9%
3 months: 3.5%
6 months: 4.1%
12 months: 3.4%

stances.summary: Notes inflation metrics show moderation in some measures
stances.quote: Trimmed mean and median a bit more tame than others.

stances.summary: Inflation elevated but core surprise downside unlikely to trigger Fed hike
stances.quote: Overall this confirms that the prices consumers pay were not just high but also rising quickly. But the incremental new information was also encouraging in the surprise to the downside in core. Not much here that should force the Fed to hike anytime soon.
